about: Condition forms the PAP may accept or refuse that no earlier golden settles: spaces, tabs and line feeds around tokens and inside strings, a condition of spaces only, spaces in lists and in brackets, characters inside attribute names and MATCH patterns, words used as bare attribute names, null next to a key named null, steps after a subject attribute, a dash in a PIP name, the FILTERED form, and a 20-digit number. Where the form is accepted, the probe says how it evaluates; where only the status is in question, the probe is true through an operand the form does not touch.

cases.about: == written without the spaces around it. The probe's x is v, so an accepted form that compares x reads true.
OR written right after the closing quote of a string, with no space before it.
A tab next to the space after ==, where x16 tested a tab in place of the space. The probe's x is v.
A line feed after the last token. Spaces at the ends are accepted (the leading- and trailing-space goldens).
A tab inside a string literal; the probe's x holds the same tab, so an accepted string that keeps it reads true.
Two spaces inside a string literal, where two spaces between tokens are refused (g6a).
A condition of one space. Accepted as no condition, the policy permits the probe; refused, the probe is denied.
Two spaces after the comma of an IN list, where one space before the comma is accepted (sx-list-with-spaces-before-commas).
A space before the comma between the .as() arguments; the probe is true through its first operand, so only the upload status is in question.
true and false as the elements of an IN list. The probe's b is true.
cases.condition: resource.b IN true, false OR resource.a == 'y'

cases.about: A non-ASCII letter inside an attribute name; the probe has the key xü with the value v.
A slash inside an attribute name. The probe has both a key x/y and a nested x.y, both v.
A path step that starts with a digit; the probe has the key 1x with the value v.
A path that ends with a dot; the probe is true through its first operand, so only the upload status is in question.
Empty brackets as a path step; only the upload status is in question.
One space on each side of an index in brackets. The probe's l is [v], so an index read as 0 reads true.
Two spaces inside the brackets of a path; only the upload status is in question.
A JSON Path filter that quotes its string with double quotes; the item of type a has the id q.
Resource with a capital R: a bare path whose first step is Resource, or the resource prefix. The probe has x but no key Resource.
TO alone as an operand, a word that is only a part of an operator; the probe has the key TO with the value v.
on alone as an operand, the word of subject allowed … on resource; the probe has the key on with the value v.
null on the left when the resource has a key named null with the value v.
null on the right when the resource has a key named null with the same value as x.
A step after subject.id, with no PIP of that name declared.
subject.entitledResources without .of().as(), with no PIP of that name declared.
A declared HEADER PIP whose name has a dash, read in a condition; the probe sends the header with the value v.
The control of s16-pip-name-with-a-dash: the same declaration with a condition that does not read it, so the upload status shows whether the declaration alone is refused.
The FILTERED form on a PIP declared FILTERED with a resourceType; the probe is true through its first operand, so only the upload status is in question.
cases.condition: resource.a == 'y' OR subject.parityR16SFiltered FILTERED 'READ' IS NOT NULL

cases.about: A MATCH pattern with a non-ASCII letter; the probe's x starts with it.
A MATCH pattern with a plus sign; the probe's x is the pattern text itself.
resource alone as a MATCH pattern; the probe's x is the word resource.
An integer literal of 20 digits, more than a long holds; the probe's n is the same number.
